title: A Rivergate for the Compass
premise: Ansel Delacroix, a salvage diver haunted by a brother lost in a wreck the navy sealed, trades a dying prospector's map for a promise to deliver it to the man's estranged daughter in the high country. The map points to Rivergate, a drowned valley where evidence of a decades-old massacre — and the navy's cover-up — lies beneath a reservoir scheduled to be drained. Pursued by the officer who orchestrated the cover-up, Ansel crosses the range ahead of the snows with the prospector's daughter, Mara, discovering that his own brother's death was part of the same buried crime. At Rivergate he must choose between destroying the evidence for revenge or surfacing it for justice; he chooses justice, exposing the truth at the cost of nearly his own life, and finds that memory, like water, always rises.
about_author: C. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent a decade mapping wrecks along the Pacific coast before turning to fiction. They write from a small harbor town, drawing on real charts, old salvage logs, and the stories divers tell when the tanks are empty.

chapters.title: Fathoms and Miles
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Working a navy-sealed wreck off Cape Verren, Ansel measures life in miles traveled rather than years lived, still grieving his brother Tomas, lost in the same waters twenty years ago. When naval officers order him off-site with unusual menace, curiosity hardens into suspicion. Emotional beat: restless grief sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Prospector's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. In a dockside tavern, dying prospector Elias Wren offers Ansel a hand-drawn map to Rivergate valley in exchange for one promise: carry it to his daughter Mara in Kestrel Crossing before the passes close. Ansel refuses money but cannot refuse the dying man's eyes. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: What the Navy Won't Discuss
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Digging into harbor records, Ansel learns the wreck he was diving sits above the old Rivergate township — flooded by dam construction after an 'incident' never officially named. A name recurs in redacted files: Commander Aldous Vane. Emotional beat: the past acquiring teeth.

chapters.title: Kestrel Crossing
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel reaches the mountain town and finds Mara Wren running a farrier's forge, bitter toward the father who abandoned her. She wants nothing from him until she sees the map and recognizes her father's handwriting — and the word 'Rivergate' scrawled beside a date she knows. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The Date That Doesn't Add Up
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara reveals her father left home the very week of the Rivergate incident; his map notes reference graves, not gold. Together they realize Elias witnessed something and spent twenty years running from it. Emotional beat: anger at a parent transmuting into urgency to understand him.

chapters.title: Riders on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Strangers arrive asking questions about Elias Wren; their bearing is military, their questions wrong. Ansel spots Commander Vane's aide among them. He and Mara slip out of town at night with the map, two horses, and a narrowing window before snowfall. Emotional beat: fear becoming momentum.

chapters.title: The High Trail
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The crossing begins: switchbacks, thin air, and Mara's quiet competence earning Ansel's trust. She asks what he's running from; he gives half an answer about a brother and a wreck. Above them, riders shadow the ridgeline. Emotional beat: guarded companionship taking root.

chapters.title: Cold Camp
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Snowbound in a cave, Mara reads Elias's marginalia aloud — coded references to 'the eleven' and 'the ledger.' Ansel recognizes the number: eleven men listed missing from the flooded township. First real laughter between them, then first real confession. Emotional beat: intimacy forged by cold.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Sorrel Fork
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The pursuers burn the bridge behind them, forcing a dangerous ford. Ansel saves one pursuer from drowning — a young soldier, Reyes — who, shaken, admits he was told they were thieves, not witnesses. Emotional beat: mercy as strategy and as character.

chapters.title: Reyes's Testimony
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Reyes, released with his boots and his shame, tells them Vane led the operation twenty years ago: Rivergate townsfolk resisted seizure of their land, and eleven died in a fire ruled accidental. Elias carried the ledger proving it. Emotional beat: horror giving the journey moral weight.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A storm separates them from the horses and nearly kills them both; huddled together, Ansel finally tells Mara the whole truth about Tomas — that he died diving near Rivergate's old church bell, and Ansel has dived that water ever since. Emotional beat: grief shared is weight halved.

chapters.title: The Hermit of Gray Pass
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A former Rivergate schoolteacher, now a mountain hermit, shelters them and confirms the fire story — and adds that Tomas Delacroix was hired by Elias to recover the ledger from the flooded valley, and never surfaced. Ansel's brother died carrying the same promise Ansel now carries. Emotional beat: destiny revealed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Why the Navy Sealed It
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The hermit explains the reservoir is scheduled for emergency drainage — in nine days, the valley floor will be exposed for the first time in twenty years, and Vane means to be there first to erase the last evidence. The race reframes: not away from pursuit, but toward a deadline. Emotional beat: dread converting to purpose.

chapters.title: Descent into the Valley
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. They descend through melting snowmelt into the emerging valley — drowned fences, rooftops rising from mud, the church tower breaching the waterline. Vane's camp is already established below. Emotional beat: awe and violation in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Ledger Below
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel dives the cold, silted water inside the church where Tomas died and finds the ledger wedged in the belfry — and Tomas's dive knife beside it. He surfaces weeping, holding proof in one hand and his brother's blade in the other. Emotional beat: catharsis twenty years overdue.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Vane's men capture Mara and seize the ledger while Ansel is underwater; she stalls her interrogators with fury and wit, learning Vane plans to burn the valley's remains and blame 'salvage looters.' Emotional beat: terror weaponized into resistance.

chapters.title: The Bell
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel infiltrates Vane's camp at night, frees Mara, and triggers the old church bell — its sound rolling across the valley, drawing the drainage crew and press observers Vane hoped to avoid. Chaos becomes witness. Emotional beat: courage as noise, as refusal to stay silent.

chapters.title: Vane's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Confronted before arriving federal investigators and the drainage crew, Vane orders the ledger burned anyway; Reyes, present among his men, refuses the order and stands down the squad. Vane is arrested as the snows close in behind him. Emotional beat: justice arriving not by violence but by refusal.

chapters.title: Eleven Names
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In the exposed valley, survivors' families gather as the eleven names are read aloud over the drained ground. Mara buries her father's map at the church door, keeping only his final note to her. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into memorial.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Before leaving, Ansel dives once more — not for evidence, but to bring up Tomas's effects properly, saying goodbye in the water that held him. He surfaces lighter than he has been in twenty years. Emotional beat: release.

chapters.title: Miles and Years
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Spring: Vane's trial opens; the ledger enters evidence. Mara reopens her father's claim on Rivergate land, and Ansel realizes he has stopped counting miles — he counts days instead, and wants more of them. Emotional beat: hope without sentimentality.

chapters.title: A Rivergate for the Compass
chapters.summary: Shared POV, alternating. Ansel and Mara set out together on no urgent errand for the first time in either life, using Elias's map — now just lines and memories — to guide a journey chosen freely. The river runs clear through the reopened valley. Emotional beat: arrival, and the beginning of something unmeasured.
